title: Fix stale-copy false positive that flags a live record
lead:
`adj lint` and `adj renumber` call a live record a stale renumber copy and tell
the owner to delete it. Two hand-named files with the same ID and name text
(`0003-foo.md`, `00003-foo.md`) collide; renumber moves one to `0005-foo.md`
with history "from 3"; from then on `IsStaleCopy` matches the keeper
`0003-foo.md` against `0005-foo.md` (other ID, same name text, renumbered from
3) and lint reports the keeper as renumber-leftover.
findings_note: S15 gate note (2) on S16; reproduced in the S16 run; S23 review notes (3), (6) on S16
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** other lint checks, renumber's planning or keeper rule
(C146), S17 dogfooding.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A lint finding that tells the owner to delete a live record is data loss
waiting to happen, and S17 (dogfood) needs `adj lint` to be trustworthy. The
same pass folds in the queued wording notes and the optional lock fallback.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/store/renumber.go` (`IsStaleCopy`, its doc comment, renumber's
  refusal) and `internal/store/renumber_test.go`.
- `internal/lint/lint.go` (`leftovers`), `internal/lint/lint_test.go`, a new
  fixture under `internal/lint/testdata/`.
- `internal/cli/lint.go`, `internal/cli/renumber.go` help text and their tests.
- `internal/store/lock_unix.go` and `internal/store/lock_test.go`.
- Docs that describe the leftover rule or the lock (AGENTS.md, docs/, README)
  where they change.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- store: a keeper with the same ID and name text as a moved record (padding
  differs) and different content is not a stale copy; the existing
  stale-copy tests (renumbered from 2 and edited since; renumbered from 9)
  still hold.
- lint: a fixture with the keeper `0003-foo.md` and a moved `0005-foo.md`
  (renumbered from 3, different content) reports no renumber-leftover; the
  existing renumber-leftover fixtures still report it.
- renumber: the same store is not refused with ErrStaleCopy.
- cli help: `adj lint --help` and `adj renumber --help` say "check both" before
  "delete".
- lock: when `.adj.lock` exists and opening it read-write fails with EACCES,
  the lock is taken through a read-only open (skip on platforms or as a user
  where the permission cannot be denied).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `IsStaleCopy` also requires the content to match: the moved record, without
   its renumber entry and with the stale ID, equals the stale file's record
   (the comparison and which fields count are the implementer's call; record it
   as a catalog decision with a one-line reason, C32). A stale copy whose
   moved record was edited after the crash must still be found; say in the
   decision how that case is told apart from a keeper.
2. `leftovers` and Renumber's refusal use the new rule; both still say "check
   both" before "delete".
3. Help text of `adj lint` (renumber-leftover line) and `adj renumber`: "check
   both, then delete".
4. Catalog wording: C155's "Create has the same gap and is not changed here" is
   superseded by C162; C162's "an invalid record still writes nothing, not even
   the directory or the lock file" is untrue for a record invalid only with its
   real ID. Correct both through slicer catalog commands.
5. Lock: if opening `.adj.lock` O_RDWR|O_CREATE fails with EACCES and the file
   exists, open it O_RDONLY and flock that; any other error behaves as today.
   Record as a catalog decision.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `. scripts/env.sh`, then `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`
  prints nothing.
- Each new test was red before the change and is mutation-checked.
- `slicer catalog list --kind decision --json --lean` has the new decisions;
  C155 and C162 read correctly.
- `slicer check --json` is clean.
